fun_highlights: The prose is consistently strong and avoids the genre's usual saccharine tone. Lines like 'Read a book he couldn't yet understand, and loved it anyway' or the affair card 'It would be so easy, and so quiet, and no one would ever have to know — which is precisely what makes it dangerous' are economical and carry real feeling. Across the opening two dynasties (Brandt, Ashby), the writing rarely lapses into the generic.

The vocation system genuinely differentiates lives. The soldier arc (service -> ghost at three in the morning -> elder truth-telling) produces a recognisably different texture from the scholar arc (hungry years -> study-pays -> legacy decision -> elder unanswered question). In the transcripts, Carys the soldier and Iris the scholar within Dynasty 1 read like different people in different worlds, which is the core ask of the genre.

Callback cards are the game's best mechanic. When Iris at 61 passes the rough sleeper and the text explicitly reaches back to 'the lonely child in the yard, the time she looked away' (cb_lookaway), or when Ren Salvedi at 49 finally reads the book from age 11 (cb_books_late), the long-arc payoff produces genuine narrative satisfaction. These are the moments that would make a player want to stay.

The dynasty layer has real texture in the opening session. The motto crystallisation ('Nothing was given; all was built' for House Brandt earned across three generations), the heirloom inheritance screen, the collateral-succession path for childless lives — these give the succession beat genuine weight rather than feeling like a loading screen. The heir-screen prose ('You are no longer Carys. You are Iris') is a small but effective identity hand-off.

Era variation gives successive founder lives a genuinely different opening feel. Dynasty 6 founder Anders Salvedi opens into a war era, Dynasty 11's Annika Okonkwo into a plague era, and Dynasty 15's Roman Lindholm into lean years — the c_origin card reads entirely differently in each, and the era-gated content (w_war_call, w_plague_tend, w_hard_winter) means the first life of each session has a distinct coloring depending on what the engine rolled.
staleness: The 'lonely child in the yard / look away' arc is almost universal. Across the 15 dynasties, looking-away-from-the-outcast-child (c_friend) fires in Dynasty 1 Iris, Dynasty 2 Edmund, Dynasty 3 Greta-skipped, Dynasty 4 Pavel, Dynasty 6 Idris, Dynasty 11 Annika, Dynasty 14 Niall, and most dynasties thereafter. The callback (cb_lookaway: 'the person sleeping rough, something very old turns over') then fires in roughly the same proportion of lives. Within a first session of 2-3 lives this recurrence is already noticeable — Iris looks away, Edmund looks away, the callback fires in both.

The 'mentor taken under a wing' card (y_mentor) and its heirloom ('the habit of teaching the young') appear in Dynasty 2 Tobias, Dynasty 4 Mercer founder, Dynasty 5 Bjornsen, Dynasty 7 Calloway, Dynasty 9 Sereno, Dynasty 12 Quint-2, Dynasty 14 Marchetti, Dynasty 15 Lindholm-2 — essentially every second life in the transcript. The mechanic is good but the frequency makes it a structural fixture rather than a memorable beat.

The opening childhood checklist feels formulaic across dynasties. Nearly every life passes through a version of: born (era line) → c_origin → c_unfair OR c_book → c_animal OR c_friend → c_move OR c_wonder → y_calling. The individual moments are written with care, but the sequence is predictable enough that by the second dynasty a player can feel the template being populated. In the transcript, compare the child years of Lazlo Bjornsen (Dynasty 5) with Cassian Ashby (Dynasty 8) — structurally near-identical despite different trait seeds.

The elder section has a strong tendency toward the same cluster of moments: health scare (m_health) → body observation lines (observe() pool) → peer-dies or m_who_became → e_garden or e_craft → e_bequest → e_legacy → e_peace. The observation prose pool is large but the observations themselves ('The stairs have started to ask a question of them' / 'The body has begun keeping its own quiet counsel') fire reliably in every life past 40, and by the third or fourth life in a session the player will have read several variants of the same body-aging note.

Epitaphs recur despite the deduplication logic. In the 15-dynasty transcript: 'Left people gentler than she/he found them' appears for Noor Ashby (D8) and Anders Salvedi (D6). 'Remembered, most of all, for a steady kindness' appears for Cyrus Ashby (D8) and Yara Okonkwo (D11). 'Taught what she/he knew, and so outlived the knowing of it' appears for Linnea Okonkwo (D11) and the D5 Bjornsen founder. The RECENT_LINES dedup fires per-session but the pool per cluster is only 5-6 lines, so a player who runs 4+ dynasties will see verbatim repeats.

The 'no fixed calling / drifter' path that fires for roughly 13% of lives produces its own monotony within itself. In the transcripts, Linnea Salvedi (D6-3), Calla Okonkwo (D11-5), and Theda Quint (D12-3) all pass through near-identical sequences: y_adrift → a_adrift_work (ache for anchor or lean into range) → m_adrift_reckon (make peace / grasp late) → e_adrift_old (count doors). The arc is structurally sound but the prose variants in those three cards are exhausted after two drifter lives.

improvements.what: Reduce c_friend / cb_lookaway frequency by raising the cooldown or adding a mutual-exclusion gate with c_animal. Currently both can fire in the same life, and the lookaway memory + callback fires in roughly 60% of lives in the transcript. The emotional payoff is strong; the problem is the saturation.
improvements.why: The 'look away from the lonely child' beat is the single most recognisable repeated structural unit in a first session. A player who has seen it twice — once choosing to look away, once triggered the callback — has essentially exhausted it. Making it genuinely rare raises its impact when it does land.

improvements.what: Deepen the childhood divergence by making the trait-affinity weighting more aggressive for the c_origin-to-first-moment transition. The current 2.6x multiplier for trait-matched cards (engine.js line 282) is not enough to make the opening 3-4 moments feel clearly different for a bookish vs a restless vs a frail child. Consider also gating c_wonder and c_book as mutually exclusive (both boost curiosity; only one should fire per life).
improvements.why: The transcript shows that the child-years checklist — regardless of trait — converges on the same 4-5 cards in the same rough order. A player beginning their second dynasty expects the template. Stronger trait divergence in the very first 10 years is what makes the second life feel fresh rather than familiar.

improvements.what: Expand the epitaph cluster pools from 5-6 lines to 8-10 per cluster, and consider allowing stat combinations to unlock hybrid epitaphs (e.g., high mind AND high spirit producing a distinct 'luminous thinker' line not reachable by either stat alone).
improvements.why: Epitaphs are the most visible per-life summary and recur verbatim in the transcript within 4-5 dynasties. They are also the last thing a player reads before deciding whether to continue — a stale epitaph signals the whole game is repeating. The code infrastructure in epitaphFor() is already well-designed; it just needs more raw material.

improvements.what: Give the drifter arc at least one distinctive mid-life moment not shared by the called arcs — a card that fires only for vocation==='adrift' and has no equivalent beat in the soldier/scholar/maker clusters. Currently a_adrift_work, m_adrift_reckon, and e_adrift_old all read as inward-monologue variations on 'what have I made of myself'; a moment that puts the drifter into a genuinely different external situation (an unusual encounter, a skill trade, a border-crossing moment) would break the solipsistic texture.
improvements.why: The drifter arc's weakness is that it is entirely internal — three decisions about how to feel about one's un-shapedness. The called arcs have external events (the campaign, the study-pays, the masterwork) that put the character into a world. The drifter has none, which makes the arc feel thin after two plays.

improvements.what: Add 2-3 more elder observation lines per pool in engine.js observe() — particularly for vit_neg (the 'body keeping its own ledger' pool at line 63, currently 9 lines). Elder lives in the transcript are long (70-90 years) and the observation pools are visibly exhausted within a single life: Niall Marchetti (D14) triggers 'He has grown courteous with his own body' at 79 and 'Mornings take longer' at 71, both in the same life's log.
improvements.why: Observation lines are ambient texture — not choices, but the prose between choices. When they repeat within a single life's log they undermine the illusion that the engine is attending to this particular person. Widening the pool to 12-14 lines per bucket would largely prevent in-life repetition.

verdict: A Life is a well-written, coherently designed meditative sim that delivers genuine pleasure in its first two lives — the prose is unusually good for the genre, the callback mechanic produces real long-arc payoffs, and the dynasty layer has enough texture to motivate succession. The score sits at 6.8 rather than 7.5+ because staleness becomes legible within that first session: by the third life a player can feel the childhood checklist populating, recognise the 'lonely child in the yard' as a structural fixture, and anticipate the elder body-decay observations as scheduled. The vocation arcs genuinely differentiate lives but the drifter arc is notably thinner than the others. The improvements needed are not architectural — the engine is sound — but are primarily about widening prose pools, reducing the frequency of the most-repeated beats, and giving the opening childhood years stronger divergence by trait.
